title: Keigo at work: answer interview questions

words.kana: しょくむけいれきしょ

parts.reading: しょくむけいれきしょ

words.meaning: an employee assigned by a staffing agency

lessons.title: An actual action, an actual result
lessons.description: Practise a concise introduction, specific experience and a purposeful question to the interviewer.
lessons.canDo: Recognise own-side interview forms and separate genuine feedback from unsupported claims.

grammar.title: Introduce yourself; describe your own work
grammar.explanation: と申します formally states your name to the interviewer. 担当しております describes your ongoing responsibility; 担当いたしました describes a completed responsibility. Choose tense from the experience rather than making every sentence more elaborate.
grammar.formation: Name + と申します. Selected 担当する → 担当しております / 担当いたしました. These are own-side forms in this interview.
grammar.mistake: Do not use おっしゃいます for your own name. Do not report a past internship as a current role.

examples.ja: {現在|げんざい}、{資料|しりょう}の{作成|さくせい}を{担当|たんとう}しております。
{実習|じっしゅう}では、{案内|あんない}の{作成|さくせい}を{担当|たんとう}いたしました。
examples.en: During my internship, I prepared guides.

grammar.title: Prospective employer: spoken and written references
grammar.explanation: 御社 refers courteously to the addressee’s company in the spoken interview; 貴社 is the corresponding written form in an application. 弊社 refers to your own company when speaking externally, so it cannot mean the employer you are applying to.
grammar.formation: Selected business nouns: 御社（おんしゃ）, 貴社（きしゃ）, 弊社（へいしゃ）. The tested contrast is company ownership and medium, not verb conjugation.
grammar.mistake: Do not call the prospective employer 弊社. The selected conventions for companies do not automatically name every school or government body.
grammar.example: 御社の仕事に関心があります。
grammar.translation: I am interested in your company’s work.

examples.ja: {御社|おんしゃ}の{仕事|しごと}に{関心|かんしん}があります。
examples.en: I am interested in your company’s work.

examples.ja: {貴社|きしゃ}への{応募|おうぼ}{理由|りゆう}を{書|か}きました。
examples.en: I wrote my reason for applying to your company.

examples.ja: {弊社|へいしゃ}では{資料|しりょう}を{作成|さくせい}しております。

grammar.title: Ask the interviewer; keep achievement and intention separate
grammar.explanation: 伺ってもよろしいでしょうか asks permission for your question. The interviewer supplies the explanation; you receive it. Say what you actually did and what you hope to do, without turning a future intention into a completed result.
grammar.formation: Selected 尋ねる/聞く → 伺う → 伺ってもよろしいでしょうか. ご説明いただけますか asks to receive the other person’s explanation; ご説明いたします offers yours.
grammar.mistake: Do not use ご説明いたします when asking the interviewer to explain. Do not invent a measured improvement when no measurement was made.
grammar.example: 研修について伺ってもよろしいでしょうか。

examples.ja: {研修|けんしゅう}について{伺|うかが}ってもよろしいでしょうか。
{最初|さいしょ}の{仕事|しごと}をご{説明|せつめい}いただけますか。
examples.en: Could you explain the initial work?

examples.ja: この{経験|けいけん}を{今後|こんご}の{仕事|しごと}に{生|い}かしたいと{考|かんが}えております。
examples.en: I would like to apply this experience in my future work.

dialogues.title: Prepare one concrete experience
dialogues.scene: After the client sample explanation, You and Mori prepare for an internal interview practice. Ishikawa will act as a recruiter; this is not a new application or hiring decision.

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: {午後|ごご}の{面接|めんせつ}{練習|れんしゅう}、{課長|かちょう}が{面接官|めんせつかん}{役|やく}をしてくれるよ。{自己紹介|じこしょうかい}は{一分|いっぷん}で。
lines.romaji: Gogo no mensetsu renshū, kachō ga mensetsukan yaku o shite kureru yo. Jiko shōkai wa ippun de.
lines.meaning: The manager will play the interviewer this afternoon. Keep your introduction to one minute.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {名前|なまえ}と{現在|げんざい}の{担当|たんとう}を{話|はな}して、その{後|あと}に{経験|けいけん}を{一|ひと}つ{挙|あ}げます。
lines.romaji: Namae to genzai no tantō o hanashite, sono ato ni keiken o hitotsu agemasu.
lines.meaning: I’ll give my name and current role, then one example of experience.

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: {白黒|しろくろ}の{表|ひょう}の{話|はなし}はどう？{自分|じぶん}が{何|なに}を{変|か}えたか{伝|つた}わる。
lines.romaji: Shirokuro no hyō no hanashi wa dō? Jibun ga nani o kaeta ka tsutawaru.
lines.meaning: How about the black-and-white table? It shows what you changed yourself.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {凡例|はんれい}と{番号|ばんごう}を{加|くわ}えたことですね。{田村様|たむらさま}は{区別|くべつ}できるとおっしゃいました。
lines.romaji: Hanrei to bangō o kuwaeta koto desu ne. Tamura-sama wa kubetsu dekiru to osshaimashita.
lines.meaning: Adding a key and numbers, right? Ms Tamura said she could distinguish the categories.

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: うん。それは{実際|じっさい}の{返事|へんじ}だね。{読|よ}む{時間|じかん}が{半分|はんぶん}になった、とは{言|い}えないよ。
lines.romaji: Un. Sore wa jissai no henji da ne. Yomu jikan ga hanbun ni natta, to wa ienai yo.
lines.meaning: Yes. That is actual feedback. You can’t say reading time was halved.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {時間|じかん}は{測|はか}っていませんからね。{料金|りょうきん}は{森|もり}さんに{確認|かくにん}してからお{伝|つた}えしました。
lines.romaji: Jikan wa hakatte imasen kara ne. Ryōkin wa Mori-san ni kakunin shite kara otsutae shimashita.
lines.meaning: We didn’t measure the time. I checked the price with you before telling her.

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: そこも{大事|だいじ}だね。{一人|ひとり}で{全部|ぜんぶ}{決|き}めたように{話|はな}さないで。
lines.romaji: Soko mo daiji da ne. Hitori de zenbu kimeta yō ni hanasanaide.
lines.meaning: That matters too. Don’t make it sound like you decided everything alone.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {最後|さいご}に、{入社|にゅうしゃ}{後|ご}の{研修|けんしゅう}について{伺|うかが}ってもいいですか。
lines.romaji: Saigo ni, nyūsha go no kenshū ni tsuite ukagatte mo ii desu ka.
lines.meaning: Can I ask about training after joining at the end?

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: いいと{思|おも}う。{練習|れんしゅう}だから、{課長|かちょう}には{応募|おうぼ}{先|さき}の{会社|かいしゃ}の{人|ひと}として{話|はな}そう。
lines.romaji: Ii to omou. Renshū da kara, kachō ni wa ōbo saki no kaisha no hito to shite hanasō.
lines.meaning: I think so. For the practice, address the manager as someone from the company you’re applying to.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {話|はな}す{時|とき}は「{御社|おんしゃ}」ですね。では、やってみます。
lines.romaji: Hanasu toki wa “onsha” desu ne. Dewa, yatte mimasu.
lines.meaning: So I’ll use onsha when speaking. All right, I’ll try it.

dialogues.title: Try a short mock interview
dialogues.scene: Ishikawa takes the role of a prospective employer for this practice. Bao uses the actual table revision and client feedback as the example, then asks about the hypothetical training.

lines.speaker: Ishikawa
lines.line: それでは、{自己紹介|じこしょうかい}をお{願|ねが}いします。
lines.romaji: Sore de wa, jiko shōkai o onegai shimasu.
lines.meaning: Please introduce yourself.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: バオと{申|もう}します。{現在|げんざい}、{資料|しりょう}の{作成|さくせい}とお{客様|きゃくさま}への{説明|せつめい}を{担当|たんとう}しております。
lines.romaji: Bao to mōshimasu. Genzai, shiryō no sakusei to okyakusama e no setsumei o tantō shite orimasu.
lines.meaning: My name is Bao. I currently prepare materials and explain them to clients.

lines.speaker: Ishikawa
lines.line: {最近|さいきん}、{仕事|しごと}で{工夫|くふう}したことを{教|おし}えてください。
lines.romaji: Saikin, shigoto de kufū shita koto o oshiete kudasai.
lines.meaning: Tell me about something you recently improved at work.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {白黒|しろくろ}では{色|いろ}を{区別|くべつ}できない{表|ひょう}に、{番号|ばんごう}と{凡例|はんれい}を{加|くわ}えました。お{客様|きゃくさま}に{見本|みほん}を{確認|かくにん}していただきました。
lines.romaji: Shirokuro de wa iro o kubetsu dekinai hyō ni, bangō to hanrei o kuwaemashita. Okyakusama ni mihon o kakunin shite itadakimashita.
lines.meaning: I added numbers and a key to a table whose colours could not be distinguished in black and white. I had the client check the sample.

lines.speaker: Ishikawa
lines.line: その{結果|けっか}、どうなりましたか。
lines.romaji: Sono kekka, dō narimashita ka.
lines.meaning: What was the result?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {番号|ばんごう}で{区別|くべつ}できるというお{返事|へんじ}をいただきました。{内容|ないよう}や{料金|りょうきん}を{変|か}えずに、{読|よ}みやすくする{方法|ほうほう}を{学|まな}びました。
lines.romaji: Bangō de kubetsu dekiru to iu ohenji o itadakimashita. Naiyō ya ryōkin o kaezu ni, yomiyasuku suru hōhō o manabimashita.
lines.meaning: The client replied that she could distinguish the categories by number. I learned how to improve readability without changing the content or price.

lines.speaker: Ishikawa
lines.line: {当社|とうしゃ}では、その{経験|けいけん}をどう{生|い}かしたいですか。
lines.romaji: Tōsha de wa, sono keiken o dō ikashitai desu ka.
lines.meaning: How would you like to use that experience at our company?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {御社|おんしゃ}でも、{使|つか}う{方|かた}の{立場|たちば}で{資料|しりょう}を{確認|かくにん}したいと{考|かんが}えております。{最後|さいご}に、{研修|けんしゅう}について{伺|うかが}ってもよろしいでしょうか。
lines.romaji: Onsha demo, tsukau kata no tachiba de shiryō o kakunin shitai to kangaete orimasu. Saigo ni, kenshū ni tsuite ukagatte mo yoroshii deshō ka.
lines.meaning: At your company too, I would like to check materials from the user’s perspective. May I ask about training before we finish?

lines.speaker: Ishikawa
lines.line: はい。{最初|さいしょ}の{一|いっ}か{月|げつ}は、{先輩|せんぱい}と{一緒|いっしょ}に{資料|しりょう}を{作|つく}ります。{二|に}か{月|げつ}{目|め}から{説明|せつめい}も{担当|たんとう}します。
lines.romaji: Hai. Saisho no ikkagetsu wa, senpai to issho ni shiryō o tsukurimasu. Nikagetsume kara setsumei mo tantō shimasu.
lines.meaning: Yes. In the first month, you prepare materials with a senior colleague. From the second month, you also give explanations.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: ありがとうございます。{初|はじ}めから{一人|ひとり}で{担当|たんとう}するのではなく、{先輩|せんぱい}と{学|まな}べるのですね。
lines.romaji: Arigatō gozaimasu. Hajime kara hitori de tantō suru no de wa naku, senpai to manaberu no desu ne.
lines.meaning: Thank you. So I can learn with a senior colleague, rather than taking responsibility alone from the start.

readings.title: Interview practice notes: contribution and next question
paragraphs: {社内|しゃない}の{面接|めんせつ}{練習|れんしゅう}のメモ。{石川課長|いしかわかちょう}が{応募|おうぼ}{先|さき}の{面接官|めんせつかん}{役|やく}を{務|つと}めた。{自己紹介|じこしょうかい}では{名前|なまえ}と{現在|げんざい}の{担当|たんとう}を{短|みじか}く{話|はな}した。
{経験|けいけん}は{白黒|しろくろ}の{表|ひょう}。{番号|ばんごう}と{凡例|はんれい}を{加|くわ}え、{田村様|たむらさま}から{区別|くべつ}できるという{返事|へんじ}をいただいた。{読|よ}む{時間|じかん}は{測|はか}っていない。{料金|りょうきん}は{森|もり}さんに{確認|かくにん}した。
{練習|れんしゅう}で{聞|き}いた{研修|けんしゅう}は、{最初|さいしょ}の{一|いっ}か{月|げつ}が{先輩|せんぱい}との{資料|しりょう}{作成|さくせい}、{二|に}か{月|げつ}{目|め}から{説明|せつめい}も{担当|たんとう}するという{内容|ないよう}。{採否|さいひ}の{通知|つうち}ではない。

recycling.reason: The real table’s 凡例 returns as a specific experience, without forcing recruitment vocabulary into every answer.

exercises.prompt: Which claim does Mori tell Bao NOT to make?
options: {読|よ}む{時間|じかん}が{半分|はんぶん}になった。
{番号|ばんごう}と{凡例|はんれい}を{加|くわ}えた。
{田村様|たむらさま}が{区別|くべつ}できると{返事|へんじ}をした。
exercises.explain: Reading time was not measured; the other events really occurred.

exercises.prompt: Who plays the interviewer in the afternoon practice?
options: {石川課長|いしかわかちょう}。
exercises.explain: Mori says the manager will play the interviewer.

exercises.prompt: What specific change does Bao describe?
options: {印刷|いんさつ}の{料金|りょうきん}を{半分|はんぶん}にした。
{一人|ひとり}ですべての{価格|かかく}を{決|き}めた。
{表|ひょう}に{番号|ばんごう}と{凡例|はんれい}を{加|くわ}えた。
exercises.explain: Bao revised the table; the price was checked with Mori and unchanged.

exercises.prompt: According to the practice answer, when does explanation work begin?
options: {入社|にゅうしゃ}{初日|しょにち}。
exercises.explain: The first month is material preparation with a senior colleague; explanation starts in month two.

exercises.prompt: Form practice: formally state YOUR own name.
exercises.explain: 申します is the own-name form; おっしゃいます respects another speaker.

exercises.prompt: Form practice: ask permission to ask the INTERVIEWER about training.
exercises.line: {研修|けんしゅう}について＿＿もよろしいでしょうか。
exercises.explain: 伺う marks the applicant’s asking the interviewer.

exercises.prompt: Answer with the actual client feedback, not a made-up measured result.
exercises.line: その{結果|けっか}、どうなりましたか。
options: {番号|ばんごう}で{区別|くべつ}できるというお{返事|へんじ}をいただきました。
{読|よ}む{時間|じかん}が{半分|はんぶん}になりました。
{料金|りょうきん}を{半分|はんぶん}にしました。
exercises.explain: The client confirmed distinction by number. No time reduction was measured.

exercises.line: {最初|さいしょ}の{一|いっ}か{月|げつ}は、{先輩|せんぱい}と{一緒|いっしょ}に{資料|しりょう}を{作|つく}ります。
options: {初日|しょにち}から{一人|ひとり}で{説明|せつめい}するのですね。
まず{先輩|せんぱい}と{資料|しりょう}{作成|さくせい}を{学|まな}ぶのですね。
{最初|さいしょ}の{一|いっ}か{月|げつ}は{研修|けんしゅう}がないのですね。
exercises.explain: The answer explicitly includes learning with a senior colleague.

exercises.meaning: May I ask about training? (Use the taught formal question.)
exercises.explain: State the topic before asking permission for your question.

exercises.prompt: Three ways: formally state your name to an external interviewer.
exercises.context: The applicant introduces their own identity or refers to the prospective employer; match the named medium and listener.
exercises.explain: と申します is the specified formal own-name introduction.

exercises.prompt: Three ways: introduce yourself to a peer in ordinary polite wording.
exercises.context: The applicant introduces their own identity or refers to the prospective employer; match the named medium and listener.
exercises.explain: です is the specified ordinary polite form.

exercises.prompt: Which company reference belongs in a WRITTEN application addressed to the prospective employer?
exercises.context: The applicant introduces their own identity or refers to the prospective employer; match the named medium and listener.
exercises.explain: 貴社 is the selected written reference; 御社 is spoken and 弊社 refers to your own company.

exercises.prompt: According to the notes, who checked the price before it was passed on?
options: {田村様|たむらさま}の{社長|しゃちょう}。
exercises.explain: The notes explicitly attribute the price check to Mori.

exercises.prompt: What do the notes say this meeting was?
options: {社内|しゃない}の{面接|めんせつ}{練習|れんしゅう}。
{採用|さいよう}を{決|き}めた{通知|つうち}。
{田村様|たむらさま}の{注文|ちゅうもん}{確認|かくにん}。
exercises.explain: Ishikawa plays the interviewer in a practice; there is no hiring notification.
